journeys.consumer: inference runtime model, graph, adapter or host-cache metadata
journeys.topology: one caller-owned 4096-entry cache; each 4096-operation replay is 93.75 percent hit-and-touch and 6.25 percent insert-and-evict
journeys.ownership: the cache owns keys and values; the caller supplies the weight and handles synchronous eviction; device transfer, pinning, in-flight state and KV policy stay above Container
demand_sources: sglang/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache storage and runtime bounded caches
journeys.peer: Abseil flat_hash_map plus std::list using the same stable hash and HYLE system allocator, storing and enforcing identical per-entry/total weight, with bad_alloc mapped to the same typed result and rollback after partial insertion
journeys.reason: bounded weighted recency storage is common across the four inference references; both adapters preserve identical entry and weight limits, recoverable failure and no-partial-commit semantics while the benchmark measures the generic storage mechanism rather than engine-specific eviction policy

journeys.consumer: inference runtime active-object, backend or registry membership
journeys.topology: one prebuilt 32768-entry set; eight persistent workers each perform 4194304 deterministic 50-percent-hit membership queries on distinct physical cores, producing a process window above 100 ms on W1-WIN
journeys.ownership: the set owns keys; construction and reserve are cold; workers receive only snapshot membership results and perform no external synchronization
demand_sources: vLLM runtime worker, block and backend registries
SGLang runtime worker, transfer and cache registries
journeys.peer: oneTBB concurrent_unordered_set with the identical stable hash, equality and HYLE SystemStdAllocator backend
journeys.reason: a payload-free set is the natural consumer shape; forcing a dummy mapped value would pollute both storage and API, while hash and allocation policy are equalized rather than hidden in defaults

journeys.consumer: inference runtime bursty task, completion or transfer inbox
journeys.topology: four persistent producers and four persistent consumers transfer 1048576 typed values through one unbounded FIFO-compatible queue; every item is checksummed exactly once
journeys.ownership: the queue owns each in-flight value; producers and consumers do not wait on a service-level close, deadline or cancellation contract; allocation failure remains explicit on HYLE enqueue
demand_sources: vllm/vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload and distributed connector SimpleQueue inboxes
sglang/python/sglang/srt mem-cache and disaggregation transfer queues
journeys.peer: oneTBB concurrent_queue using HYLE SystemStdAllocator, with bad_alloc mapped to the same recoverable enqueue result
journeys.reason: bursty unbounded typed handoff recurs across inference runtimes; allocator and OOM results are equalized, while blocking policy and process transport remain intentionally outside the container

journeys.consumer: model, path and process metadata crossing a UTF-16 host boundary
journeys.topology: 256 independent valid mixed-ASCII and multibyte 128-byte metadata records are validated, sized and converted into caller-owned UTF-16 storage
journeys.ownership: input and output are caller-owned; HYLE allocates nothing, reports malformed input and required output exactly, and never exposes provider types
demand_sources: llama.cpp/common/common.cpp and tools server/rpc UTF-8 path conversion
vLLM and SGLang model/token metadata entering native and operating-system boundaries
ds4 GGUF and host metadata boundaries
journeys.peer: the product-locked simdutf implementation pointer performing validate-with-errors, exact length and endian-correct convert-valid, adapted to the identical UtfResult
journeys.reason: the comparison charges the same safe caller-buffer contract on both sides, including malformed input and output-too-small oracle checks; raw unchecked transcoding is not an equivalent peer

negative_space.policy: KV eviction, pinning, in-flight ownership, request scheduling, tokenizer automata and device placement remain engine or upper-module policy
negative_space.queues: wait, close, deadline, cancellation, backpressure and process transport belong to Sched or IO rather than Container queue storage
negative_space.unicode: filesystem I/O, locale policy, normalization and owning string allocation are outside caller-buffer transcoding
negative_space.performance: Python queues and policy caches prove demand but are not C++ timing peers; each P1 row uses a mature source-pinned C++ implementation under SAME_CONTRACT
negative_space.ordinary_containers: std and PMR remain the natural route for ordinary vector, string, deque, node map and heap tasks
